derivation: Generated by tools/import_kicad_board.py from the vendor's own KiCad footprint. Pad centres are exact to three decimal places in millimetres, scaled at 8.0 px/mm from a 20.91 x 24.55 mm extent including a 1.0 mm margin. Pin names joined from the symbol library on pad number. Nothing here was measured off an image.
assumption: Every `pin` is null: that field is the rcontrol pin index of a PICSimLab board implementation (webui/pinmap.py), and none exists for this board. `chip_pin` and `chip_index` are what tools/import_pindefs.py read out of the board-support packages named in `pindefs`; a pad whose `chip_pin` is null says why in `why_null`. webui/boards/samd21.py reads a level through the same table, so a pad with a `chip_pin` answers for itself in the pin view; a pad without one is drawn and reported as not modelled. 11 pins on this board are named with NO flat number -- PA02, PA04, PA10, and so on -- so every pad reaching one carries `chip_index` null for that reason and not for a missing reading: no flat GPIO numbering is published for the SAMD21 at all, so webui/boards/samd21.py keys its own table by port and bit instead, and derives `PIN_NAMES` from that.

pindefs.derivation: Generated by tools/import_pindefs.py from the board-support packages in `packages`, at those revisions. Nothing was inferred from the CAD, the silkscreen or a pinout image: a label resolves only when every package covering the board that defines it names the same pin, and `python tools/import_pindefs.py <board>` prints the file that named it.

pads.label: SWDIO
pads.why_null: the SWD debug interface, which Seeed's own page for this board names: Seeeduino-XIAO.md says '1 SWD pad interface'. No pin number for it is published anywhere in this tree -- no board-support package file this tool reads for this board mentions SWDIO or SWCLK, and Seeed publish no board CAD for this part as they do for the RP2350 and both nRF54s. NOT claimed: whether the chip has a GPIO behind this pad, which no file here states
